column1: # ABI check on the pinned toolchain (rustc 1.99.0, rust_preserve_none_cc), Apple M4:
preserve_none_args
column2: a `extern "rust-preserve-none" fn pn(a,b)` called from asm with x20=7 x21=9 x0=1 x1=2 returns 709, so preserve-none maps arg0->x20, arg1->x21 (rows: frame x20, ctx x21, pinned ints x22..). A `extern "C"` entry (entry_body) takes x0=context x1=receiver x2=captures x3=window and the thunk moves them to x21/x20, so both image entries agree with the row map

column1: image_callee_unresolved
column2: the failing step arrives with the helper's four words (6, 4, tagged(3), tagged(3)); the caller's own steps read vm/residual/lane_context correctly; the image function symbol is the entry_body thunk (unit_0_function_0 starts with the x19..x30 save then `mov x21,x0; mov x20,x3; bl first`), so the call ABI and the entry agree and the defect is in the context word the calling row hands over

column1: # Call-row instrumented (enrollment preserved, c1.js):
no_helper_call
column2: `body_call_helper` printed nothing for c1.js while its callee faulted, so the callee is entered by a direct/stitched call row, not the helper; `osr_lane::enter` printed nothing either, so no OSR region runs in this path: the failing step is inside an ahead body of the image
column3: CALL_HELPER count 0, REGION_PAYLOAD count 0 over the whole c1 run

column1: caller_payload_ok
column2: the caller's four steps read vm=0x16ff0f720 residual=0x7000006650 lane_context=0x16ff0cd28 (a bound `JsStepDispatch`: at70=0 before binding, at78=residual, at128=lane_context); the callee's first step then reads vm=6 residual=4 lane_context=tagged(3), and its call_pc hole is tagged(3) too — values shaped like a `LoopEntry`/window record, not the dispatch
column3: BIND dispatch=<heap> at70=0 at78=7000006650 at128=<lane_ctx>; then STEP … 6 4 tagged tagged

column1: payload_repoint_no_effect
column2: making `BodyRunContext::bind_run` re-point `context.adapter_payload` at its own dispatch on every entry changed nothing (c1/v4 still 139, r1/ty2/loop exact), so the callee is not entered through `bind_run` at all — it is a direct native call whose context comes from the calling row
column3: c1/v4 exit 139 after the change; r1 n=20000, ty2 n=20000, loop n=20000

column1: next_probe
column2: wrap the image base body's entry (`LaneMethod::of_linked_base`) in an `extern "C" fn` that logs (context, receiver, captures, registers) once and forwards, to see exactly which context the call row hands the callee

column1: # Why the corpus loops stay interpreted (osr-reject, 2026-11-21):
loop_reject_env_local
column2: a loop that reads a top-level `let` (an environment binding) is refused whole: `iterates_natively` cuts the DFS at any op that does not lower in a loop, and LoadEnvLocal is one
column3: op_call.js: `UnsupportedInstruction(7), pc: 8` where pc 8 is LoadEnvLocal; Basic.js: `UnsupportedInstruction(9), pc: 4` five times, plus 56/73/82

column1: corpus_shape
column2: because a harness script declares `function Benchmark()`, its top-level `let`s live in the environment, so the timed loops read env locals and are refused; the whole loop then runs in the interpreter (op_call 40 ns/op, 176 instructions)
column3: op_call.js vs op_add.js (no nested function, `s` in a register: 0.61 ns/op, loop compiled)

column1: base_admits_leaving_loops
column2: `admit_region` refuses the loop only under the Cranelift tiers: `if !base_only() && iterates_natively(...)`. BaseJIT admits a loop that leaves every iteration (a call, an unsupported op) and lowers it row by row — which is why deltablue 2.4 s and raytrace 9.6 s with Base beat 5.8 s and 16.4 s without it

column1: base_entry_bug
column2: Base's mid-loop entry restarts the *induction* at 0 while every other register keeps its value (n=20000+k, s=6*n); entering at 0 (floor-rows) is exact. Fixing that entry is what lets Base return and carry the corpus loops

column1: # Base promotion handoff probe (ty2.js, Tier::Base temporarily re-enabled):
base_promotion_handoff
column2: the Base region does not mis-enter: it runs in chunks of exactly 4807 backedges and leaves with `LaneExit::Terminated` (the promotion budget), four times, then `At(12)` with 0 iterations; the loop's n ends 245 ahead of i, so the over-count is in the promotion/safepoint handoff, not in the induction load (the OSR probe shows r16=s=6*i, r17=n=i, r18=i at each entry: 1017, 5824, 10631, 15438)
column3: REGION_EXIT exit=Terminated iterations=4807 ×4, then At(12) 0; OSR from=4 r16=0x…17d6 r17=r18=0x…3f9 (i=1017)

column1: ultra_exact
column2: with the Base tier out (the committed policy) the Ultra region is exact on the same program and reads 0.64-0.86 ns/op on the micro-suite; every corpus loop it refuses is refused because of a non-lowering op in the body, not because of the induction

column1: # Env-local admission (2026-11-21): the reject is the tagged-register analysis, not the loop check.
env_local_trait
column2: LoadEnvLocal lacked BOXED_RESULT while LoadCapture/LoadName/GetField have it, so `tagged_registers_with_failure` refused the loop (`LIFETIME_BLOCKED op=LoadEnvLocal pc=8`). Adding the trait makes the loop compile (a Cranelift region, 1216 bytes, no leave, 19,960,798 iterations in one run)
column3: bytecode.rs LoadEnvLocal traits; osr_loop.rs tagged_operand -> carries_boxed

column1: env_local_lowering_cost
column2: but the compiled loop is 4x slower than the interpreter: three call_indirect per iteration (env-local read, the callee, env-local write) -> op_call 157 ns/op against 39 ns interpreted

column1: reverted
column2: the trait change is reverted until the env-local access lowers natively: rows are neutral (navier-stokes 490 vs 502, deltablue 4266 vs 4285, Basic 4451 vs 4458) but any hot loop that touches a top-level `let` would pay the 3 calls

column1: # Module mode: identical source, CJS 2.2x slower than ESM (2026-11-21)
module_mode
column2: the same call-loop source (op_call.js) runs 39 ns/op as `.mjs` and 86 ns/op as `.cjs`; the repo's package.json has "type": "module", so repo paths are ESM and /private/tmp paths are CJS. Node is 0.586 (mjs) / 0.295 (cjs), Bun 1.031 / 0.217, so the mode costs us 2.2x and them nothing

column1: module_mode_shape
column2: both compiled a loop region (ESM header=7 1216 bytes, CJS header=6 1344 bytes) and both call the callee from an environment local that holds a MakeClosure result (function 0/1 pc 0 MakeClosure, loop `LoadEnvLocal; Move; Call`); the CJS region is larger and slower

column1: row_harness
column2: all row entries live in /private/tmp/opencode/aot (CJS), so the row numbers are the CJS regime; Node and Bun read the same files, so the ratio is fair

column1: # The region is the slow path for a loop with a call (2026-11-21, probes on a.mjs/a.cjs)
region_vs_lane
column2: the same call loop is 39 ns/op when the Ultra region declines at the environment-local read (`REGION_EXIT exit=At(8) iterations=0`, five times) and 86 ns/op when the region runs the loop in one chunk (`At(12) iterations=19947861`): the compiled region does the call through its step helper (call_indirect) and is 2.2x slower than the lane/interpreter it replaced
column3: a.mjs 39.6 ns vs a.cjs 86.2 ns, same source, same CLIF work (527 vs 542 lines, 2 call_indirect each)

column1: tier_model_gap
column2: `iterates_natively` admits any ordinary call under `MethodCalls::Inliner` optimistically; the lowering then steps it when the inliner does not take it, so the region runs a call it cannot inline. A call the inliner cannot take must block the region (or leave at the call), not become an in-region step

column1: # Image vs JIT after the v2-merged merge and the region's call leave (2026-11-21):
image_equals_jit
column2: the compiled image is now as fast as the JIT on the same source: Basic 4337 (jit 4283), deltablue 4230 (4319), navier-stokes 479 (483), raytrace 7241 (7448) ms. The earlier "image 2-2.5x the default per-op cost" no longer holds; the remaining gap to Node is the runtime's per-op cost, not the image path

column1: leaf_callee_not_claimed
column2: `pays_native_entry` needs 20 records (`JS_TIER_LANE_ENTRY_RECORDS`), so a 4-record leaf callee like `f(x) = (x+1)|0` never gets a body; the lane runs it as a leaf call at 8.7 ns/op where Node inlines it at 0.3. Promoting a callee after many unclaimed entries is the missing rule (the tier model decides before any call count is known)

column1: # Leaf calls bypass the tier (2026-11-21, code + measurement):
leaf_is_terminal
column2: `lane_run_leaf` enters the callee's records in the lane and never calls `tier_enter_in_lane`/`js_tier_activation_entry`, so a leaf callee's entries are never counted, it never warms, and it never gets a body; the site's `CallEntry` also stays the leaf form, so even a published body would not be called. That is why "warm an unclaimed function by entries" was inert (9.46 vs 9.43 ns/op) and why the call cannot become compiled on this path
column3: lane_run_leaf / lane_enter_leaf / leaf_arm in dispatch_fast/leaf_calls.rs; tier_enter_in_lane is only on the activation prologue

column1: call_path_forward
column2: the call reaches Node's cost only by compiling it in the caller: inline the leaf callee's records into the Ultra region at plan time (the stitcher's `inline::InlineSite`, whose absence is why Base was faster on calls), or emit a per-callee native leaf thunk. A leaf callee body/hot-entry rule cannot help while the leaf row stays terminal

column1: # Base region entry, tested with promotion off (2026-11-21):
base_entry_restarts_induction
column2: with `Tier::Base` back in the default mode and `promotion_taken` forced to None (so the region runs whole, no handoff), the stitched region still restarts the induction: ty2 n=29295, sw4 n=29295 s=40283310, ty4 n=29484 — the over-count equals the interpretation before the region's first entry, so the handoff was not the cause. The earlier "induction is seeded right" probe (OSR r18=i=1017) measured the *Ultra* path, when Base was out of the default mode

column1: base_is_not_usable_until_entry_fixed
column2: so Base's leaf inlining (the one mechanism that already makes calls cheap) cannot be used until the stitched entry reads the live register file; Ultra has no leaf inlining at all (no `leaf` in lane_region), which is the feature the call budget needs
column3: lane_region.rs has no leaf path; call_plan/inline.rs is the stitcher's

column1: # Stitched entry probe (Base + promotion off), ty2, first entries:
stitched_entry_reads_right
column2: the stitched region's entry reads the live register file correctly on its first entry (slot 17 = n = 1017, slot 18 = i = 1017, slot 15 = s), so the induction is not lost at the entry; the over-count happens inside the region's run (later entries show i = 19999 with n = 29491, i.e. n advanced while i sat at the loop bound)
column3: OSR_ENTRY regs=0x7004015b08 r17=0x7ffd…03f9 r18=0x7ffd…03f9, then r17=…7333 r18=…4e1f

column1: stitched_merge
column2: so the two defects are separate: the entry's register file is right, and the stitched region's own merge/exit of the loop-carried induction (or its leave at a callout) advances n without i. Base stays out of the default mode until that is found; Ultra is exact

column1: # Forcing every tier does not inline the call (2026-11-21):
floor_rows_worse
column2: `QUENCH_DEV=floor-rows` (every eligible site compiles at its first chance) makes the call loop worse, not better: a.cjs 37.7 ns/op against 9.4 normally, a.mjs 65.7 against 38.8. So engaging the tier more eagerly (the body tier, the loop body tier) does not inline the callee; `QUENCH_TRACE=js-jit` also reports `tracked_functions: 0` for these programs, so no body is planned at all

column1: region_inlining_is_new_code
column2: `lane_region` has no leaf path and an OSR region is lowered from `osr_loop::region` (instructions + sites), not from a `lane_unit::Unit` with `InlinedCall` frames, so inlining a leaf callee's records in a region is new lowering code: identity guard, parameter mapping into the window, record splicing, the `Return` completion and every leave inside it. Nothing existing does this for the Ultra tier

column1: # Leaf call cost is dispatch, not work (2026-11-21): f(){return 1} 7.52 ns, f(x){return x} 7.18 ns,
# f(x){return (x+1)|0} 8.60 ns. The setup (row dispatch, fill_admitted_window, copy_arguments,
# enter_leaf, complete_leaf) is ~7.2 ns of the 8.6; the callee's records add ~1.4.
leaf_dispatch_dominates
column2: the per-call cost is interpreter dispatch, so neither a cheaper body nor a hotter callee helps: only a compiled call removes it

column1: region_inlining_locations
column2: the Ultra region's unit is `osr_compile::loop_unit(function)` with `frames: Vec::new()`; `lane_region::lower` already consumes `unit.frames` (`InlinedCall`, `Origin::Inlined`, `callee_entry_word`), and `lane_unit::with_trips(targets, trips, body)` is the planner that makes frames (used by bodies at lane_compile.rs:400). The remaining work is (a) plan the region's call sites into frames in loop_unit, and (b) extend the region's `Coverage::Loop { header, backedge }` to the frames' unit PC ranges, which today lie past the caller's instructions and would be lowered as exits

column1: # Env-local callee inlining (2026-11-21): planned but declined at run time.
env_local_frame_planned
column2: admitting a `LoadEnvLocal` callee with `InlineGuard::AtRead` (source `Register`, the read kept) does plan the frame: `region.inlining=true`, `unit.frames.len()=1` for both a.cjs and a.mjs. But a.mjs stays at 38.5-38.9 ns/op with and without it, so the inlined plan is not what runs: the frame's recovery is `Materialize`, and a frameless lane activation admits no room for it (`region_admits_in_lane`/`frame_holds_window_in_lane`), so the region falls back to the plain unit plan. a.cjs is unaffected (0.53-1.10 with, 0.54-1.03 without).
column3: QUENCH_PROBE_INLINE print; a.mjs/a.cjs before and after

column1: env_local_reverted
column2: no measured benefit, so reverted; the env-local shape needs the recovery room a materializable inlined frame takes, not a different guard

column1: # Env-local shape is not a room problem (2026-11-21): `region_admits_in_lane` returns true for a.mjs
# (no REGION_DECLINE print), and the region leaves at its environment-local read every iteration
# (`REGION_EXIT exit=At(8) iterations=0` repeatedly), pc 8 being `LoadEnvLocal`. The frameless lane
# activation for the module body has no environment storage, so the read's step leaves at once.
env_local_leave_not_room
column2: the ESM call loop's 38.9 ns/op is the region leaving at its callee read (pc 8, 0 iterations) each iteration, not an admission decline: `region_admits_in_lane` is true and no room growth is needed. Reserving `callee.registers` would not change it; the read itself has to run (the activation has no environment storage for the module body's `let` bindings)
column3: REGION_EXIT At(8) iterations=0 x6; no REGION_DECLINE output

column1: rows_are_cjs
column2: the 36 row entries are CJS (`/private/tmp/opencode/aot` has no package.json), where the copied-Move inlining already runs the call at 0.55 ns/op; the env-local shape only affects ESM harnesses, so it is not what holds the rows back

column1: # Where the big rows spend their time (2026-11-21, probes):
hash_map_regions
column2: hash-map compiles one body and four loop regions (header=22, 2.4-3.0 KB each), but the whole run makes fewer than 2000 region runs and the first exits `At(32)` with 0 iterations: the loop leaves on its first row every time and the work is interpreted, not compiled

column1: raytrace_one_region
column2: raytrace compiles exactly one loop region and no body in the whole run (`jit-dump`: `loop header=1` only), so its per-iteration work runs interpreted

column1: claim_gate
column2: the claim gate at a resolved call is `!lanes || tier_unclaimed_in_lane` and `tier_may_claim`; for raytrace's call targets `tier_may_claim` is false for most (the function is under `JS_TIER_LANE_ENTRY_RECORDS` and has no loop) and true for a few (fn 43, 46), yet no body publishes. `js_jit_lane_methods_enabled()` is false on this path (a restored startup snapshot resets the program store), but preserving it across the restore changes nothing measurable (raytrace 7340 vs 7306, hash-map 10562, richards 6158, Basic 4360), so the missing tier is the claim/body path itself, not the flag

column1: # Body tier on the JIT path (2026-11-21): the claim fires, the lane tier is off at run time.
claim_fires
column2: `claim_for_tier` runs for raytrace's fn 43, 46, 21, 59, 61 and the prologue record runs (`PROLOGUE fn=43 lanes=false` many times), but `specialize_in_lane` never runs and no body is planned (`SPECIALIZE`/`BODY_WORK` never print): with lanes false, `tier_enter_in_lane` skips `specialize_in_lane` and falls to the numeric tier, which refuses the non-numeric functions (raytrace's take objects).
column3: probes in claim_for_tier, tier_prologue_resumed, specialize_in_lane, body_work_in_lane

column1: lanes_false_after_compiled
column2: `Runtime::set_execution_mode(Compiled)` does run (`SET_MODE mode=Compiled`) and enables lane methods, yet the prologue reads `lanes=false` afterwards: the program store that carries the flag is replaced between the two (a snapshot restore builds a new `ProgramStore`), so the lane-body tier is off for every JIT run. The next probe is to print in `ProgramStore::enable_js_lane_methods` and at each `ProgramStore::read_snapshot` to name the replacement.

column1: # Lane-body tier: my own patch disabled it; enabled it publishes bodies that leave at once (2026-11-21).
self_disabled
column2: `ProgramStore::enable_js_lane_methods` still carried the `#[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")] return;` added when the ty2 call-continuation bug appeared, so the lane-body tier was off in every mode and every `PROLOGUE ... lanes=false` observation was that one line. Removing it (all reproducers and differentials exact: ty2 n=20000, r1 20000, sw4 199990000, ty4 mism=0, inl 20000,399980000,50000,100000,20000, with s=140000 n=20000, args t=99005050) makes raytrace publish six bodies (functions 2, 5, 43, 46, 59, 61).
column3: raytrace jit-dump with the line removed

column1: bodies_leave_immediately
column2: those bodies do not pay: each leaves at its first row, 64 times (`QUENCH_BODY_LEAVE function=43 exit=At(1)`, fn 46 At(1), fn 59 At(2), fn 5 At(9), fn 2 At(5), fn 61 At(1)), i.e. every entry leaves at the first op the body cannot run, so the rows regress (raytrace 7429 -> 8196, richards 6228 -> 8425, hash-map 10430 -> 11626, Basic 4450 -> 4713, deltablue 4227 -> 4972) and the tier stays off until those first rows lower.
column3: row measurements with the line removed then reverted

column1: # Why every published body leaves at its first row (2026-11-21): the first rows are `Construct`.
construct_blocks_bodies
column2: raytrace's bodies leave at pc 1/1/2/5/9 and each of those pcs is a `Construct` (`new Vector(...)`): fn 43 pc 1, fn 46 pc 1, fn 59 pc 2, fn 2 pc 5, fn 5 pc 9; fn 61 leaves at pc 1, a `GetField` on a capture. `lane_region` has no construction arm at all (only a `construct_ready` field for virtual objects), so a body cannot run past its first `new` and every entry falls back to the interpreter.
column3: bytecode dumps of fns 2/5/43/46/59/61 vs the At(pc) leaves

column1: construct_is_the_key
column2: raytrace allocates a Vector at the head of essentially every helper (intersect, testIntersection, addScalar, renderScene), so lowering a proven construction in the body — the interpreter's `construct_in_lane` plan, or a call-out that continues at the next record — is what lets the lane-body tier pay at all

column1: # The real gate on a body's first call: `raises_from` (2026-11-21).
construct_is_a_call
column2: `Construct` decodes as `Operation::Call(CallOperation::Site)` with `site.constructs()` (operation.rs 586, invoke.rs 69), so it is not a missing lowering: lane_region has the call arm, including a `raised` block (`raised_call`). What blocks it is the line above: `let origin = self.unit.origins.get(pc).filter(|_| self.raises_from(pc))`.

column1: unwind_gate
column2: a call is only made natively where the body can unwind from it: a handler covers the pc, or the pc is a recorded leave (`leaves_at`, from a previous plan's feedback). Otherwise the body leaves *before* the call, and the lane makes it. For raytrace every helper starts with `new Vector(...)`, so every body entry leaves at pc 1/2/5/9 before doing anything; after 64 such leaves per body nothing has run and no usable leave is recorded, so the body never becomes useful — enabling the tier only pays for compiles.

column1: next_fix
column2: let a body make a call it cannot unwind from and leave the lane at the call's record when it throws (the `LANE_BODY_THREW`/`Raised(pc)` path already exists): that is the semantics the interpreter has, and it lets a body that begins with `new`/a call run its whole body instead of surrendering at the first row

column1: # The chain end to end (2026-11-21): a body cannot make a call whose callee has no body.
call_needs_callee_body
column2: removing the `raises_from` filter (so a body makes a call and leaves the lane on a throw) changes nothing: the bodies still leave at At(1)/At(2)/At(5)/At(9), because the call lowering now leaves when the callee has no published body (the change that made the CJS call 0.55 ns). For raytrace every callee is a constructor or a small method with no body, so no body can proceed; enabling the tier just pays for compiles (raytrace 8239, richards 8544, hash-map 11599, Basic 4769, deltablue 4932 against 7394/6129/10432/4347/4227)
column3: raises_from filter removed + tier enabled, measured then reverted

column1: body_must_step_calls
column2: so a body is useful only if it can *step* a call it cannot inline or call directly (a call-out that continues at the next record), which image bodies already do (`fill_stepped_miss`); the lane-body path has no such fallback, only inline/direct/leave. That is the missing piece for the tier on this corpus
column3: lane_region's call arm: inline (frames), direct (published body), else leave

column1: # The step-call fallback works but loses (2026-11-21).
step_fallback_runs
column2: allowing `stepped_record` for lane bodies (drop the `LaneHelpers::Ahead` gate) does give bodies the call-out fallback: leaves move past the first row (raytrace fn 43 now leaves `Callee` 1489 times and `At(5)` 64, fn 46 `Callee` 391 + `At(23)` 96, instead of every entry leaving At(1)); the reproducers and differentials stay exact

column1: step_fallback_loses
column2: but it is far slower (raytrace 10817 vs 7320, gaussian-blur 3528 vs 1687, deltablue 4964, hash-map 10804, Basic 4635) and richards panics: a body that steps every call through the interpreter's helper pays more per call than the interpreter's own loop, so a body is only worth compiling when its calls are *inlined* or *direct to compiled bodies*. Reverted.

column1: # Escaping-construction lowering: the pieces that exist (2026-11-21).
construct_plan_machinery
column2: `virtual_construct_plan(pc, instruction)` already resolves a construction's `ScalarConstructPlan` from the VM's site plans (`vm.construct_plans(function, at)`), and `ConstructPlanHolds` is the helper the region calls once per loop to prove the plan still stands (`hoist_constructions`, `ConstructReady`). `virtual_construct` then runs the construction by the plan, but keeps the object *virtual* (fields in registers, no record): `materialize_virtuals` makes a record only when the value escapes, and a construction whose result escapes is not taken by this path at all, so the body leaves at it.

column1: construct_design
column2: to make an escaping `new C(args)` run in a body: (a) guard `ConstructPlanHolds` at the site as the virtual path does, (b) allocate the record from the plan's shape/header (`MakeObject`-class row with the constructor's shape), (c) bind `this` to that record and run the constructor by its direct entry when it has a body, or inline its stores (the `Origin::Inlined` frames already used for calls); (d) on a miss, leave *before* the allocation as today. The pieces are `ScalarConstructPlan`, the object-row allocation in `object_slots`/`constructions`, and the frame machinery; only the escaping allocation and the constructor run are new

shapes_reduce_leaves\twith `entry_shapes(program, unit, fields)` + `prove_entry_shapes` (one `object_header` + `prove_header_shape` per never-written receiver; the failed check leaves through the entry's shared `LaneExit::Entry`), raytrace fn 46's first leave moves from `At(29)` to `At(7)` and the reproducers stay exact (ty2 n=20000, r1 20000, sw4 199990000, ty4 mism=0; inliner 20000,399980000,50000,100000,20000).\tQUENCH_BODY_LEAVE before/after

Skipping the per-read compare on that proof can then read a stale slot. The region path is safe because it compares the shape at every read. # Typed-array loops: the kind dispatch is the cost (2026-11-21).

ta_dispatch\ta loop with two typed arrays of different kinds (gaussian-blur: Uint32Array source, Float32Array line) gets `ElementViews::Typed(None)` (`ElementViews::common` keeps a kind only where both name it), so every element access emits `typed_elements::by_word`'s linear chain of `eq_imm`+branch over the 9 native kinds, plus a bounds test and a `sadd_overflow` per index step. In ta_f32's compiled region the executed chain is 26 blocks for one pixel; measured 6.19 ns/op against Node's 1.98, and gaussian-blur's own loop 25.9 ns/pixel against Node's 2.9.\tmicro/budget-typed.tsv; code-001.clif block chain 61..227

ta_loop_is_native\tthe row's cost is not entry overhead: the outer region runs a whole pass natively (`REGION_EXIT header=10 exit=At(103) iterations=450`, 22 entries for 25 passes) and the same micro is 30x its interpreter (181 ns/op no-jit), so the loss is per-access code inside the loop.\tREGION_EXIT probe on op_ta_f32/op_gauss_inner

ta_fix_direction\tper-array kinds at plan time: an array the loop only reads has its kind observed (`number_reads`/`ElementViews`), so its arm can be `ViewKind::Static` (one arm, no chain); a write-only array's kind is proved per array at the entry (`prove_typed_view_into` defines `variables.kind`), so the dispatch can compare the proved word once and select the arm by it. Either removes 4-9 compares per access from the row's hottest loop.\tstaged/typed_elements.rs by_word, lane_region.rs hoist_typed_view/prove_typed_view_into
# Per-array typed kinds landed (2026-11-21): gaussian-blur 1698 -> 1418 ms.

per_array_kinds\teach loop array now keeps the typed kind its register held at entry (`Observation::typed_kinds`, sampled by `loop_tier::typed_array_kinds` through `Vm::typed_array_kind`, keyed by the access's operand register and its resolved source): `LoopArray::views` is `Typed(Some(kind))`, so an access keeps one arm instead of walking `typed_elements::by_word` over the 9 kinds. gaussian-blur 1698 -> 1418 ms (16%), ta_f32 6.19 -> 5.14 ns/op, ta_read 2.59 -> 1.75, navier-stokes unchanged (487), all reproducers and differentials exact.\tmicro/budget-typed.tsv

what_remains_in_the_pixel\tthe inner loop is now 18 CLIF blocks with 15 branches per pixel (5 bounds checks, 4 `sadd_overflow` index steps, the loop test) against Node's 1: the next cost is the per-access bounds test and the int32 overflow check on `line_index + k`, which a range proof over the row (`line_index < 4*width`) would hoist.\tcode-001.clif of ta_f32 after the change

array_kind_differential\tthe per-array kind is taken only from a register the loop does not write; the keyed-by-operand path is gated on `!written.contains(base)`, so a register reassigned inside the loop (a copy chain) falls back to the resolved source's entry kind. default, --no-jit, node and bun all read 55000,20003.5,29993.000.\tmicro/op_array_kinds.js
# Bimodal rows (2026-11-21): sha256 and pbkdf2 alternate between a compiled and an
# interpreted run, which makes their sweep values a coin flip, not a regression.

bimodal_rows\tstanford-crypto-sha256 reads 1785 / 1575 / 5871 ms on three consecutive runs of the same binary, and stanford-crypto-pbkdf2 5346 / 1603 / 5373 (the same commit, same source): either the hot region publishes and enters inside the timed section, or it does not and the row runs interpreted. Neither is caused by the per-array kinds (re-measured at 554b2cdaf6 and 03e4babc84: 1773 and 1762 ms for sha256, and 5891 at HEAD with the kind application disabled), so the cause is when the loop tier's compile lands, not the code it makes. Any row's sweep number on these two is one of the two modes until that is made deterministic.\tthree runs each, same binary

remaining_branches\tper pixel the loop still emits 5 `fcvt_to_sint_sat` (a Number index converted to an int32: `fabs` + `fcmp` + `fcvt` + `ireduce` and two branches each), 4 `icmp ult` bounds tests and 5 `sadd_overflow` steps for `li + k`. next_facts_seed\tso the next change is a facts seed, not the versioning: at a loop header a register whose value before the loop is an int constant and whose only in-loop definition is an integer add of an int constant is int32 (with its range), which removes the per-access Number->int conversion and leaves the bounds/overflow tests to the versioning work above. A wrong seed is checked at the read (the int row leaves), so it is safe.\tfacts::analyze / seed_loop_ints
